# The Agent Loop Problem: When “Smart” Won’t Stop

## How to diagnose runaway agent behavior — and design guardrails that turn infinite loops into predictable, shippable systems.

Modexa

--

Listen

Share

The Agent Loop Problem explains why AI agents get stuck in infinite cycles — and how to stop them using budgets, state machines, evaluations, and safe fallbacks.

You ship an agent. It works in demos.

Then production happens.

A user asks a slightly messy question, the agent calls a tool, reads the result, calls another tool… and suddenly it’s been 47 steps and you’re staring at logs that feel like a haunted diary:

“I should verify again.”  
“I should re-check the source.”  
“I should confirm one more time.” [...] ## 1) No explicit definition of “done”

Humans have an internal “good enough.” Agents don’t — unless you give them one.

If the prompt says:

The agent isn’t broken. It’s obeying.

## 2) Unreliable tools + naive retry logic

If a tool is flaky (timeouts, rate limits, partial responses), an agent will interpret that as:

“Try again, but slightly differently.”

Without a cap, it becomes a slot machine.

## 3) Ambiguous goals and shifting targets

When a user request is unclear, an agent can bounce between interpretations:

Goal uncertainty creates loop pressure.

## 4) Context gets worse every step

Each step adds tokens: logs, partial plans, tool outputs.

Eventually the agent is reasoning over a messy transcript of its own confusion.  
And confusion feeds more confusion.

results.content: sitting there. And here is the cleanest way I have seen it broken down. A real loop has three parts that matters. And if you understand these three, you understand loops better than almost anyone on your timeline. First, verify. This is the heart of the whole thing. After the AI does the work, something has to check it. Not the AI checking itself. A real outside check. Does the code actually pass the test? Is the number above the target? Did it meet the spec? Because without a real check, you don't have a loop. You just have AI agreeing with itself on repeat. The model that did the work is way too generous a creator for its own homework. The check is the thing that turns running over and over into actual progress. Second, state. This is what makes it learn. Every pass, the AI has to [...] like playing chess. One careful move at all time. All your focus on the board. A loop is building the chess engine. You set the goal, you set the rules, and you let the machine play. This isn't tool upgrade. It's a role change. But, not all loops are the same. There are basically four flavors, and knowing which is which is half the skill. First, the heartbeat loop. It runs constantly every few seconds or minutes. You can use it for monitoring, watching logs, checking if something is healthy, scanning for problems. Think of it as a nurse checking vitals for every 5 minutes. Second, we have is the cron loop, scheduled for set times, every weekend at 10:00 a.m. Great for routine batch work, a daily review, weekly audit. Think of it as the newspaper landing on your porch every morning. Third, [...] Here, it is mentioned that after eight turns, if it still fails, it should stop.
